## What is a robotic soldering solution?

A Soldering Robot is a fully automated system that performs a designated task, set by a custom program, with the utmost precision and repeatability. Features include custom soldering profiles per joint, 150-watt power supply with thermal feedback, optional nitrogen systems and vision alignment.

## What are the advantages?

1. **Return on Investment** — Customers often achieve a ONE YEAR Return on Investment.
2. **Less Rework** — Eliminates human error, reduces defects.
3. **Highly Efficient** — Minimal operator involvement; one operator can supervise two robots; dual-tip capability available.
4. **Versatility** — Supports HMP and lead-free soldering; customizable options including nitrogen sleeves, vision guidance, safety enclosures.

## What We Offer

Systems include: IS Series (in-line integration), Table-Top Robot Series (most popular), Pro Model Series (premier line). Standard features: 150W minimum power supply, automatic solder feeder, tip cleaning station, positive tip location. Optional: nitrogen kits, safety enclosures, vision alignment.

title: Post SPI Sorting Conveyor
description:
PROMATION's NRC Series sorting conveyors inspect printed circuit boards following SPI inspection procedures. The system receives PASS/NG signals from the SPI machine after each inspection cycle. When a failure signal is received via SMEMA protocol, the PCB halts in front of an operator, and a finger mechanism lifts the failed board for examination while allowing passing PCBs to continue underneath. After inspection, operators can leave the board in place or manually remove it. Depressing a foot pedal returns the finger assembly to its starting position. If a PCB is detected, SMEMA enables continued transfer; absence of a PCB triggers conveyor reset. The station operates as a standard conveyor in pass mode, providing full end-to-end transfer capability.

Note: The PCB in fail mode is lifted over the top of the edge belt. Actual clearance is dependent upon top side height of components passing underneath the lifted PCB and if there are any bottom side components on the lifted PCB.

description:

In the world of soldering, the thermal feedback loop is one of the most critical and important features on the soldering system. All soldering irons feature a real-time thermal feedback loop while offering quick and easy solder tip replacement. The thermal sensor is positioned at the end of the solder tip's contact point to provide excellent communication and accurate thermal feedback to the power supply. 

Our heating element uses a special induction coil. When this coil is flooded with high-frequency AC a magnetic field is generated. The magnetic beam travels through our magnetized rod (sensor) to generate an induction current. This current changes the density of magnetic field and generates heat. The heating current has a thermal effect that allows the tip to quickly heat and maintain temperature (as shown in the chart). The result is an “Eddy Current” that provides .excellent temperature control throughout the entire soldering process.

Power supplies and soldering irons are offered in a multitude of different wattage and styles; ranging from 90 Watt solutions - up to 320 Watt Solutions. .

Here at PROMATION USA the concept always remains the same; to provide a superior thermal feedback loop while maintaining the "lowest cost of ownership" in its class. Our expert team can assist in directing your application towards the very best heating technology and robotic solution.
